mission: Secure AI Project designs and lobbies for state and federal laws aimed at the largest AI developers: mandatory published safety and security protocols, whistleblower protections, incident reporting and, next, independent third-party assessment and a government body able to intervene. It co-sponsored California's SB 53 and has worked on bills in nine states.

key_work.title: California SB 53 (co-sponsor)
key_work.plain_summary: First US law requiring the largest AI developers to publish and follow safety plans, report critical incidents and protect whistleblowers.

key_work.title: How California Can Meet the Moment on Frontier AI Safety
key_work.plain_summary: SAIP's legislative recommendations for California covering scope, independent verification, standards, government orders and pacing.

funding_note: Funded by individual donors and nonprofit institutions; does not accept corporate or foreign-government funding (About page).

warnings.text: Current laws only require transparency; companies decide for themselves how to respond when their systems show dangerous capabilities — as many already have.
No law yet requires a third party to assess whether an AI company's work endangers the public.
No government agency has clear authority to intervene if a dangerous AI system appears.

recommendations.text: Legally require major AI developers to publish and follow safety and security protocols.
Add independent third-party assessment and give a government agency authority to intervene.
